## Reconciled Decisions # Support agent hal.v1 subprotocol offer | Field | Value | | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Feature | Support agent hal.v1 subprotocol offer | | Issue | re-cinq/Otto#192, #203 | | Status | In Progress | | Created | 2026-09-29 | | Epic | E4 - OLT support agent | | Milestone | M2 - PoC on fixtures | | Builds on | [support-agent-foundation](../support-agent-foundation/spec.md) (#13); `044` (the chat client's WebSocket connection); HAL Engine: hal-engine-subprotocol-marker (#64) | A browser WebSocket cannot set an `Authorization` header, so the support agent's chat client carries its access token in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. HAL Engine 0.3.0 no longer echoes that token back: it answers only the reserved marker `hal.v1`, so the token stays out of the handshake response and off the socket object. For one minor release it still accepts a bare-token offer, and the release after that refuses one: that is 0.5.0, which `apps/api` adopted with #203 and now requires as `^0.8.0` (#316, #297). This feature moves the support agent to offering `hal.v1` beside its token. It ships in two parts, because `apps/api` and `apps/web` are separate Deployments that roll out independently. The api part lands first and accepts both shapes, so a browser holding the old bundle keeps connecting while the new one rolls out; the web part then changes what the client offers. Offering the marker first against an api still reading the first value would authenticate as the literal `hal.v1` and refuse every connection. ## Sources - re-cinq/Otto#316, as corrected on 2026-10-13. - HAL Engine 0.6.0: `transport/ws/conversationList.js`, `types/messages.d.ts`, `infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoSessionStore.js`. - Bowman UI 0.3.0: `components/ConversationList.d.ts`, `components/AppShell.d.ts`, `components/AppSidebar.d.ts`. ## Out of Scope - PO-reference lookup (`GET /orders?reference=` and `GET /shipments?reference=`) is not in the first cut of `get_booking_status`. Both paths exist under the same two scopes (`orders:read`, `shipments:read`) and can be added later without a new API key. Until then, an input matching neither `^OLT-\d{4}-\d{4}$` nor `^SHP-\d{4}-\d{6}$` renders the not-found card. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_fbfe6bc6-537f-4321-a68e-c36c9c3fe228), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_b1abb0fc-25b9-41bc-b1e6-b9d8771887df)) - Generating types from OpenAPI; `components.schemas` is empty. - Passing the orchestrator's `AbortSignal`, on `ToolContext.signal` since HAL Engine 0.5.0, on to the TMS request so an abandoned call stops; the crash guard reads it only to tell an abandoned call from a crash (FR-082b). - Renewing an expired credential mid-conversation (a queued HAL Engine issue). - The authentication-model decision and binding the authenticated customer to each call ([support-agent-tms-access](../support-agent-tms-access/spec.md), #15, #18). - Recording anything real: `KU-02` is open, so no fixture contains TMS data. - The evaluation harness (`KU-03`), which measures answers, not HTTP; it shares the fixture directory and nothing more, and judging whether an answer is good Danish or correct belongs to it. - Mocking the model: a separate seam, already broken (`providerFactory.ts` discards the mock's `structuredResponses`), with its own queued issue. - Building any tool beyond `get_booking_status`; each `tool` row of the question map emits its own issue, and each tool issue authors or records its own fixtures under these rules. - Amending the tool contract from the question map. - Real endpoint and response fields beyond `mapping.ts`'s guarded constants. - Fixing HAL Engine's `round <= maxToolRounds` off-by-one and its silent budget exhaustion (a queued HAL Engine issue); a consumer passing `maxToolRounds: 5` today gets six. - Rendering `tool` entries in the UI. - The Danish system prompt, the disclosure sentence, and the system prompt's domain context, which reads the question map in a separate issue. - Human-in-the-loop confirmation of consequential calls (E5), and the escalation destination for mutation rows (undecided, its own issue). - Any `hal-engine` or `bowman-ui` change for the crash guard; that work is confined to `apps/api`. - The engine's backstop, its substituted sentence and its log line, which #138 shipped and which remain the answer for any consumer that does not wrap. - A `beforeToolCall` or after-tool hook in `hal-engine` for crashes; #138 declined it because the executor is the consumer's own function, and the crash guard is that answer built at the consumer layer. - Model-call failures, owned by a sibling `model_call_failed` trigger; a provider outage and a tool crash are different failures on different seams. - What the customer reads in Danish, owned by the translation and notice-string work downstream. - Delivering the escalation to a human, which flows through the existing, unchanged escalation sink. - Typed `TmsError` mapping inside the crash guard; the factory already returns a classified result that never reaches it. - Email as an inbound channel (out of PoC scope; chat only). - The other two agent use cases scoped separately: invoice and pricing anomaly detection, and self-billing automation. - Sample support emails (`KU-04`), which give tone rather than the question list.
// FR-014: advisory only - from HAL Engine 0.3.0 a run ends at stream_end or a close, never at an error frame. function recordError(state: ChatState, frame: Extract): ChatState { // Before its connected frame a socket has no run: HAL Engine sends this before closing 1011 when it cannot set up the session. if (state.connection !== 'open') return state; // useHalChat holds a question until the list answers, so an error while the list is out is the list's. if (state.listPending) return refuseList(state); return {...state, error: {code: frame.code, interrupted: isAnswerCutOff(state)}}; } // FR-033/FR-034: more answer after an error proves the stream survived it; once the run ends the verdict is final. function releaseInterrupted(state: ChatState): ChatState { const {busy, error} = state; if (!busy || !error?.interrupted) return state; return {...state, error: {...error, interrupted: false}}; } export interface ChatState { entries: ChatEntry[]; busy: boolean; error: ChatErrorInfo | null; sessionId: string | null; examplePrompts: string[]; connection: ConnectionState; notice: ChatNotice | null; // Per connection: every connected frame sets it, so a verdict never outlives the socket it arrived on. resumeFailure: ResumeFailure | null; protocolViolations: number; // Server indices of the current session the engine suppressed (§5.5); they never reach the client array. skippedServerIndices: number[]; // A restarted session counts from 0 again, so its entries land after the transcript kept from the previous one. sessionStartPosition: number; // Where the latest question's run begins, so an earlier finished answer never reads as cut off. runStartPosition: number; conversations: ConversationListState; // Set by each connected frame, whose list_conversations the hook sends, and cleared by its answer or a close; an error while it is set answers it. listPending: boolean; // Sessions the customer asked in from this tab, kept listed though the list read on connect still counts them empty. askedSessions: string[]; // A held question the close dropped, for the composer to offer back; the transcript never showed it. unsentQuestion: string | null; } // A refused list renders nothing rather than an empty state, which would tell the customer they have no conversations. function renderConversations(chat: HalChat, close: () => void) { const {conversations, sessionId, busy, connection, openConversation} = chat; if (conversations === 'unavailable') return null; return (
{ close(); // A streaming answer arrives on the socket a switch closes, the active row is already on screen, and FR-217 holds after a failed reconnect. if (!busy && connection !== 'error' && picked !== sessionId) openConversation(picked); }} labels={danishConversationListLabels} />
); } // FR-043/FR-048: outside the transcript, whose indices the server owns, and not a Toast, which connection notices own. function renderFailure(error: ChatErrorInfo | null) { if (error === null) return null; return (
{resolveFailureMessage(error)}
); } // An error frame names no request, so a question waits for the list's answer and every error while it is out is the list's. class ListFirstOutbox { private listPending = false; private held: string | null = null; // receive and send say whether a question went out, which is what marks its session asked in. receive(frame: ServerFrame, socket: HalSocket): boolean { // One list per connection: the engine never pushes, and only a new connection can change the answer. if (frame.type === 'connected') { this.listPending = true; socket.send({type: 'list_conversations'}); } if (!this.listPending || (frame.type !== 'conversation_list' && frame.type !== 'error')) { return false; } this.listPending = false; const question = this.reset(); if (question === null) return false; socket.send({type: 'user_message', content: question}); return true; } // Until the next connection's list is in, as after any connected frame. hold(): void { this.listPending = true; } send(content: string, socket: HalSocket | null): boolean { if (this.listPending) { this.held = content; return false; } socket?.send({type: 'user_message', content}); return true; } // Returns a question still held, which the close then reports as not sent. reset(): string | null { const dropped = this.held; this.listPending = false; this.held = null; return dropped; } } export function withDeniedChatRoute(engineApp: RequestListener, config: Config): RequestListener { const chatsPath = `${config.transport.basePath}/chats`; return (request: IncomingMessage, response: ServerResponse) => { /* v8 ignore next -- request.url is always defined for real HTTP requests */ const url = request.url ?? ''; const {pathname} = new URL(url, 'http://otto.invalid'); if (request.method === 'POST' && (pathname === chatsPath || pathname === `${chatsPath}/`)) { response.writeHead(HTTP_NOT_FOUND); response.end(); return; } engineApp(request, response); }; } import type {ClosedConnectionState} from './chatReducer.js'; import {HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL} from './protocol.js'; import type {ClientFrame, ServerFrame} from './protocol.js';
